### Fixed
- **Triton's kernel cache lives on the cache claim beside vLLM's compiled graphs: the redirect rule sets `TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/vllm-cache/triton` on the runtime container** (giantswarm/agent-platform#572). Triton — the compiler behind every `@triton.jit` kernel a model runs, the GDN and Mamba kernels of the hybrid architectures among them — keeps its compiled kernels and, with vLLM's default `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING=1`, its autotuning results in `~/.triton/cache` inside the container, gone with the pod. A preset that compiles had them on the claim already: at compile init vLLM redirects `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` in-process to a directory under `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`'s `torch_compile_cache/`. A preset that serves `--enforce-eager` — six of the shipped ones — never compiles, so that redirect never ran and every pod recompiled and re-autotuned its kernels during the profiling run. The redirect rule now sets `TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/vllm-cache/triton` in the same patch as `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`: a directory of the claim's `.vllm-cache` beside `torch_compile_cache/`, which Triton creates as the runtime's uid under the setgid `root:1000 2775` directory exactly as vLLM creates `torch_compile_cache/`; a compiled preset is unchanged (vLLM's redirect takes over at compile init, the env is the floor for what Triton compiles before it), and a pod without the cache keeps Triton's default as it keeps vLLM's. `make verify-model-serving-policies` holds both envs on the runtime container of both shapes, both under the cache mount, and neither on a pod without the cache. README "vLLM's compile cache and Triton's kernel cache on the claim".
